newsitem.title: USA: Judge issues preliminary ruling against Norelco.
newsitem.headline: Judge issues preliminary ruling against Norelco.

text.p: A federal judge has ruled in favour of Gillette Co. in the first round of the shaving company's court battle with rival Norelco Consumer Products Co.

Judge Reginald Lindsay of the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued a preliminary injunction against Norelco's advertisements which claim that electric shavers cause less irritation then razor blades.

Lindsay ruled that the ads must include a "sufficiently conspicuious and contemporaneous statement" that a user of Norelco's Reflex Action electric razors should not expect less irritation until after three weeks.
Gillette claims the Norelco ads are deceptive, and has sought punitive and other damages.
In one of the television advertisements, a razor blade spits out fire. In another, the handle of a razor coils like a snake, and a forked tongue flicks out between a double-blade.
